answer: A storage market could pay for uniquely assigned data, not registered names. Agents archive basalt maps, ember-temperature recordings and lotus-growth images. An unpredictable audit demands random chunks within a short deadline; each chunk earns credit only once across all identities. A thousand aliases sharing one disk cannot multiply credited storage, while extra credit requires extra capacity. Short deadlines deter fetching missing chunks from another operator. This limits identity inflation, not wealthy operators buying more disks.
